name: Scene Medley
description: Five demos in one patch (Kaleido Tunnel, Molten Orbit, Prism Drift, Hyperbolic Lanterns, Aurora Fjord) switched by a Scene Switcher with per-scene transitions and ScenePresence-driven entrances and exits. Only the shown scene is evaluated (two while blending), so the GPU cost follows the scenes on screen, not the scene count. Auto-advances every 8 bars with music, every 12 s without. Keys 1-5, or the Scenes section in the Parameters panel (P).

data.label: Scene
data.description: Shown scene (the Scenes section above and keys 1-5 do the same)

data.label: Music reactivity
data.description: How strongly every scene reacts to the audio

data.text:
## Music
One reactivity control for all scenes (each scene keeps its own audio / beat nodes). With no audio the beat clock free-runs, so the scenes still pulse.

## Show Control
The Scene Switcher shows one scene and blends two during a transition.
- Scene / Next scene Params, keys 1-5, the Scenes section of the Parameters panel or MCP set_scene pick the scene
- Auto: every 8 bars while music (or the metronome) drives the beat clock, else every 12 s
- each scene sets its own entrance style (data.scenes[i].transition)

data.label: Scroll speed
data.description: How fast the tunnel streams toward you.

data.text:
## Tunnel Mapping
Screen UV → polar (angle, radius). 1/r gives depth, which twists the rotation; the kaleidoscope folds the angle, and depth + time scroll the cells toward the viewer.

## Voronoi Cells
Voronoi on the tunnel coordinates: glowing cell centers, animated edge rings (sin + smoothstep) and a second Voronoi layer for sparkle.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the piece looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Beat: the kaleidoscope twists forward and the tunnel lunges toward you on each beat, then both glide back (Beat Surge: eased, net zero per beat).
- Bar: the palette swings ahead on each downbeat and drifts back over the bar.
- Bass: the glow rings breathe (up to +30%).
Beat-phase couplings (beat twist and lunge, bar palette swing) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence and by Beat.gate (amount = drive x confidence x gate): confidence (u_beatConfidence) is 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome; gate is the stable beat clock's certainty (u_beatTrust): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and the surges fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (bass ring glow) are not.

# 1 · Kaleido Tunnel
Copied from the Kaleido Tunnel demo (everything up to its tonemapper). A hypnotic kaleidoscopic tunnel: polar coordinates with a 1/r depth mapping scrolled by time, kaleidoscope folding with a depth twist, and glowing Voronoi cells, finished with echo trails and bloom.
- Presence -> Kaleidoscope amount: the mirror folds open as the tunnel enters and collapses back to a single view as it leaves (style "self": the switcher only adds a crossfade).

data.label: Melt
data.description: Smooth-union radius: how much the torus and the sphere fuse.

data.label: Orbit speed
data.description: How fast the camera circles the scene.

data.text:
## Scene SDF
One signed distance function: torus ∪ orbiting sphere with a smooth union (k = melt), displaced by 3D Perlin noise, plus a floor plane. Raymarch walks each ray until this distance is ~0.

## Material / Shading
Lambert + Blinn-Phong lighting, a cosine-palette iridescence driven by Fresnel and height, and a procedural tile pattern for the floor. A step on the hit height picks floor or object.

## Environment
What rays that miss see: a vertical sky gradient, a striped retro sun drawn in screen space, and a distance-fog mask that fades surfaces into it.

## Composite & Post FX
Surfaces are mixed into the environment by the fog mask, then ACES tonemapping, saturation, vignette and film grain.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the piece looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Kick: the orbiting sphere swells (radius 0.55 → 0.68) and the molten noise churns harder (×1.6).
- Bass: the melt radius breathes up to +30%, so torus and sphere fuse more.
- Beat (attack-decay envelope): the floor grid lines flare (×2.4) and the iridescent rim brightens.
Beat-phase couplings (grid flare, rim brighten) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (BeatEnvelope gate: fade, or x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in the shaders): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (kick swell, molten churn, bass melt) are not.

# 2 · Molten Orbit
Copied from the Molten Orbit demo (everything up to its tonemapper). A raymarched torus and an orbiting sphere melt into each other over a tiled floor, under a synthwave sun.
- 1 - presence -> Dither amount: the synthwave orbit crunches into a 3-level ordered dither while it is not fully shown. Entrance: zoom through.

data.label: Melt
data.description: Smooth-union radius between the torus and the sphere.

data.label: Dispersion
data.description: RGB split of the refracted rays.

data.text:
## Scene SDF
Torus ∪ orbiting sphere with a smooth union, plus a little 3D Perlin noise on the surface. GlassRaymarch refracts through this distance field.

## Glass Shading
The environment is sampled three times along slightly different refracted rays (one per RGB channel) for dispersion, tinted by absorption, then a reflection, a cosine-palette thin film driven by Fresnel and a Blinn-Phong specular are layered on top.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the piece looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Beat: a pulse of light rolls down the synthwave grid and lands at the camera on each beat (inside Synth Env, also seen in reflections and refractions).
- Bar: the sun stripes open up and the sun brightens on each downbeat, easing back over the bar.
- Bass: the thin-film glow of the glass breathes (+20%) and the bloom threshold drops (0.85 → 0.76).
Beat-phase couplings (the grid pulse and sun bar inside Synth Env) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (BeatEnvelope gate: fade, or x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in the shaders): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (bass film glow and bloom threshold) are not.

# 3 · Prism Drift
Copied from the Prism Drift demo (everything up to its tonemapper). A molten glass blob with RGB dispersion and thin-film iridescence over a synthwave world, finished by a multi-pass post pipeline.
- Entrance: displacement (the previous scene's colors warp the glass as it fades in).

data.label: Flight speed
data.description: How fast the camera flies through the honeycomb.

data.label: Cone intensity
data.description: Brightness of the volumetric light cones.

data.text:
## Cell Geometry
Cube size, cone angle and echo (how much each reflected cell keeps) of the honeycomb, plus the centered screen UV the camera rays start from.

## Lantern Palette
Two lantern colors whose hues drift slowly with time (Hue Shift by time × 0.015).

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the piece looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Beat ripple: inside the honeycomb, each beat is delayed by distance (ripple = 0.35 beats per unit), so a wavefront rolls outward: lamp cores and cube edges flare, the light cones light up in a shell, and the cubes surge forward in their spin.
- Bass: light-cone intensity breathes up to +35%.
Beat-phase couplings (the ripple flare, cone shell and spin surge inside Hyperbolic Honeycomb) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (BeatEnvelope gate: fade, or x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in the shaders): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (bass cone breathing) are not.

# 4 · Hyperbolic Lanterns
Copied from the Hyperbolic Lanterns demo (everything up to its tonemapper). Ray tracing in hyperbolic space: the order-5 cubic honeycomb {4,3,5}, a spinning cube in every cell casting volumetric light cones.
- 1 - presence -> RotateUV / ScaleUV amount: the lanterns spin in from far away and settle (rotation 0, zoom 1) when fully shown; they spin back out as they leave. Entrance: iris.

data.label: Aurora brightness
data.description: Overall glow of both aurora curtains.

data.text:
## Water Reflection
Below the horizon the UV is mirrored and wobbled by FBM ripples (WaveUV), so the whole sky and mountains reflect in the fjord; the water then gets a dark tint.

## Aurora
Two curtains: a domain-warped FBM defines each curtain's wavy bottom edge; above it, exponential falloff × vertical FBM rays × a color ramp (green → violet) give the glowing drapes.

## Mountains
Three FBM ridgelines (far, mid, near) cut out silhouettes with smoothsteps, each shaded with haze, snow and rim light, layered front to back over the sky.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the fjord looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Mids: the aurora curtains glow up to +30%.
- Highs: the domain warp deepens (strength 0.5 → 0.56), so the drapes ripple with hats and cymbals.
- Beat: the bright stars twinkle (×2.4, short attack and decay).
Beat-phase couplings (star twinkle) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (BeatEnvelope gate: fade, or x smoothstep(0.25, 0.75, u_beatTrust) in the shaders): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (mid glow, high ripple) are not.

# 5 · Aurora Fjord
Copied from the Aurora Fjord demo (everything up to its tonemapper). A night fjord under domain-warped aurora curtains: layered FBM mountain silhouettes, twinkling Voronoi stars, low mist, and everything mirrored in rippling water.
- 1 - presence -> Grayscale amount: the aurora colors bloom in out of a gray night as the fjord dissolves in, and drain away when it leaves.

## Render Targets
Feedback nodes used as render targets: the tonemapped frame (for chromatic aberration) and a bright pass (luma smoothstep) for bloom and streaks.

## Bloom
Two blur radii of the bright pass added together, plus a tinted horizontal anamorphic streak.

## Post (shared)
One graded frame, bright pass, two-level bloom, anamorphic streaks and lens FX for every scene (copied from Hyperbolic Lanterns). Its Feedback passes run in main, so they always run; Feedback passes inside a scene would be skipped while that scene is hidden.

# Scene Medley
Five demos as scenes of one patch, switched by a Scene Switcher. Only the shown scene is evaluated (two during a transition): each scene's exclusive sub-graph compiles into its own GLSL function, called through uniform branches, so 5 scenes cost about as much as 1.
- each scene group ends in Scene Out: ScenePresence (0 hidden .. 1 shown) drives effect amount inputs for its own entrance and exit
- transitions: crossfade, dissolve, wipe, iris, zoom, push, slide, luma, displace, pixelate, self, sequential, custom
- try keys 1-5, the Scenes section of the Parameters panel (P), or let it auto-advance with the music
